message:
feat(update): fit the payload-name lock to the door it was made for

The name rules landed a commit ago, but nothing fed them a name from a
manifest. A lock that is not on a door keeps nobody out.

Manifests now carry payload names -- repeatable payload= lines, ignored by
older readers under the existing unknown-key rule -- and load_manifest checks
every one of them before it will hand back a VerifiedManifest. So an unsafe
name cannot exist inside a verified manifest, which means a caller building an
install config from one cannot receive it either. There is no path that
produces it.

That separation is the point. A signature says the bytes are ours. It does not
say the names inside them are safe, and treating it as though it did is how a
signing key or a tricked publisher turns into a write outside the install
directory.

Order is preserved because the swap moves files aside in it, and a reordering
would change which backup a rollback restores from.

Names arrive as UTF-8, so there is a UTF-8 path now. Anything outside ASCII is
refused rather than decoded: every name this product ships is ASCII, and
admitting more would mean reasoning about normalisation forms and homoglyphs in
a string that is one step from being a path.

The new cases all run with a verifier that accepts, so the only thing rejecting
them is the name check -- traversal, mixed separators, absolute, UNC, alternate
stream, reserved device, trailing dot, case-different duplicate, non-ASCII --
and each asserts no VerifiedManifest comes back. Names that should pass are
there too, so this cannot quietly become an over-block. And an unsafe name with
a bad signature still reports SignatureInvalid, which shows the new check did
not creep ahead of the old one.

Still missing, and worth being plain about: the manifest can now name files
that no package format exists to carry. Swap still copies one artifact to every
name.

qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening. Manifest suite 41 to 65 checks, 550
across the eight.
